source.title: Alarm 254 Spindle Motor Overheat
source.raw_text: [Music] if you're in the middle of a job and you get alarmed 2:54 spin the motor overheat here are a couple things you can do the spindle motor has a temperature sensor built into it usually in the junction box there are temperature limits for the spindle motor that's preset from the factory if the spindle motor temperature begins to reach those limits this sensor triggers alarm to 54 to begin with check that the spindle loads are not way over a hundred percent for long extended periods because you're running a long super-aggressive program this alarm can be triggered if there are problems with the spindle fan the fan should turn on as soon as the spindle starts turning if the fan is working make sure it's running in the right direction on a vertical mill it should pull air up through the spindle head and push it out through the top on a horizontal mill it pushes air out through the back of the spindle head if the machine has a next-gen Control open the control cabinet and look at the cable connected to p39 on the i/o PC board it should have a ferrite filter on it remove the spindle head cover and examine the temperature sensor itself make sure that it's not damaged and the cable is firmly connected if the alarm persists it's time to contact your local hospital outlet for assistance thanks for watching [Music]

source.raw_text: [Music] if you're in the middle of a job and you get alarmed 2:54 spin the motor overheat here are a couple things you can do the spindle motor has a temperature sensor built into it usually in the junction box there are temperature limits for the spindle motor that's preset from the factory if the spindle motor temperature begins to reach those limits this sensor triggers alarm to 54 to begin with check that the spindle loads are not way over a hundred percent for long extended periods because you're running a long super-aggressive program this alarm can be triggered if there are problems with the spindle fan the fan should turn on as soon as the spindle starts turning if the fan is working make sure it's running in the right direction on a vertical mill it should pull air up through the spindle head and push it out through the top on a horizontal mill it pushes air out through the back of the spindle head if the machine has a next-gen Control open the control cabinet and look at the cable connected to p39 on the i/o PC board it should have a ferrite filter on it remove the spindle head cover and examine the temperature sensor itself make sure that it's not damaged and the cable is firmly connected if the alarm persists it's time to contact your local hospital outlet for assistance thanks for watching [Music]
